Every firm communication is labeled Action Needed or Informed. Use plain, warm, specific language.

blocks.html: Lesson 6 of 7. Some messages are for one project team. Others need the whole firm's attention. This lesson gives you a simple way to label and route them.

Step 1: Action Needed or Informed?

  • Action Needed. Someone has to do something: complete a task, change a habit, update a system, or adopt a new behavior. This is a baseline expectation, not optional.
  • Informed. No immediate action. It's awareness: policy background, context, or where the firm is headed.
Every communication is labeled Action Needed or Informed. Put the tag at the start of your subject line or post: [ACTION NEEDED] or [INFORMED]. If a message isn't labeled, ask the sender.

Step 2: Choose the channel

Ask: Does this need a record, a response, or a meeting?

ChannelUse it forDon't use it for
Outlook emailExternal parties (clients, vendors, partners); anything that needs a formal record or paper trail; formal decisions; firm-wide announcements that need acknowledgmentInternal project coordination, quick internal questions
Teams channel postInternal group work, project discussion, day-to-day decisions, sharing files and linksClient communication, firm-wide announcements
Teams private chatFast, informal questions to one or two peopleProject collaboration and decisions
Ninety.io HeadlineAnything the whole team should see or align on at the next all-team meeting: wins, issues, firm-level updatesUrgent same-day items, one-on-one conversations
SharePoint (the OneAccord Hub)Official reference material you read: policies, resources, trainingAnything that needs a response or decision

A rollout can use more than one channel, for example a Ninety.io Headline to raise it at the meeting and a reference document on the Hub afterward.

Posting a Ninety.io Headline

Headlines go to the monthly all-team meeting. Keep them short: a headline is a prompt for discussion, not the full explanation.

  1. Go to the relevant meeting agenda in Ninety.io.
  2. Find the Headlines section for that meeting.
  3. Click + Add Headline (or the "+" next to Headlines).
  4. Paste in your headline, with the Action Needed or Informed tag at the start.
  5. Save. It will appear in the meeting agenda for the next meeting.

Example: INFORMED: Closed the Nelson engagement two weeks early, and the client asked about a follow-on scope. A minute at the all-team meeting is plenty.

Questions about Ninety.io? Ask Abby.

Events

Post upcoming events in the #Events channel in Teams. If you also want to alert the team, announce it in whichever channel fits: a Ninety.io Headline for team alignment, or a Teams post for a reminder.

blocks.prompt: "Starting Monday, all timesheets must be submitted by 5 PM Friday." How do you label this?
options: Neither; it doesn't need a label
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. People must do something, so it's Action Needed.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Someone has to act, so it's Action Needed.

blocks.prompt: "Here's the background on why we moved to a new CRM." How do you label it?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. It's context with no action required.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: It's background only, with no action, so it's Informed.

blocks.prompt: Where does a win you want recognized at the all-team meeting go?
options: A private chat with your manager
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Wins go in a Ninety.io Headline.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Wins are shared as a Ninety.io Headline for the all-team meeting.

blocks.prompt: A policy change needs everyone to formally acknowledge it. Which channel fits best?
options: A reaction on a channel post
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Firm-wide messages needing acknowledgment go by email.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: A formal record of acknowledgment calls for email, labeled Action Needed.

blocks.prompt: You want to announce an upcoming internal training session. Where do you post it?
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Upcoming events are posted in the #Events channel.

blocks.prompt: Which best describes a good Ninety.io Headline?
options: A long, detailed explanation with attachments
Short, tagged Action Needed or Informed, and a prompt for discussion at the meeting
A private note to one person
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Headlines are short prompts for team discussion.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Headlines are short, tagged, and meant to prompt discussion at the meeting.

blocks.prompt: A message arrives asking you to do something, but it isn't labeled. What do you do?
options: Assume it's Informed and ignore it
Assume it's Action Needed and start immediately
Ask the sender whether it's Action Needed or Informed
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Yes. If it isn't labeled, ask.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Unlabeled messages should be clarified: ask the sender.

blocks.promptHtml:
You found a client-onboarding shortcut that cut setup time in half. You want the whole team to know about it and start using it.

Decide how you'd share it, how you'd label it, and draft the short Headline text.
rubric: Labels the message correctly: Action Needed if people are expected to adopt it, or Informed with a reason if it's only awareness
Chooses a Ninety.io Headline to raise it at the all-team meeting
Drafts a Headline that is short, starts with the tag, and prompts discussion
Names a fitting follow-up channel, such as a #Lessons post with details
blocks.coachContext: Every communication is labeled Action Needed (someone must do something) or Informed (awareness only). A Ninety.io Headline is for items the whole team should see or align on at the monthly all-team meeting; it should be short, start with the tag, and prompt discussion. Details or a write-up can follow in #Lessons (or as reference material on the Hub via Jesse or Abby).
